summary: Iteration 42 production bug fix verified. Members Directory payload is now 36109 bytes (measured) versus the reported 2.6 MB before, well under the 200 KB ceiling. No character portrait_url in the /api/public/members-directory response starts with 'data:' — all are null or short '/api/image/{id}' URLs which serve 200 with image/* content-type. Owner upload to POST /api/characters/{id}/upload-image returns portrait_url starting with '/api/image/', that URL serves an image, and the character document is persisted with the short URL (no base64). Non-owner upload is rejected with 404, anonymous with 401 as expected. AuthContext resilience verified via web UI: after visiting /members, the localStorage token persists and navigating to /dashboard does NOT redirect to /login (no spurious logout). Admin and non-admin /api/auth/login + /api/auth/me regression still passes. 7/7 pytest cases green.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py exceeds 3000 lines; consider extracting the public/members-directory + /image/{id} endpoints into a dedicated module (routes/public.py). Not blocking, but the file is well past the 700-line guideline.

The defensive base64→object-storage migration inside get_members_directory runs synchronously in the request path per legacy portrait; today it's a no-op because the DB is already migrated (payload = 36 KB), but if a legacy user ever re-imports a data-URI portrait via update_character (PUT /api/characters/{id}), it would slip through and get migrated on next directory hit. Consider also gating update_character to convert data: URIs at write time so no request path pays that cost.

rca of the issue: Original prod bug: /api/public/members-directory shipped multi-MB base64 portrait_urls inline (measured 2.6 MB; 2.5 MB from a single portrait). Single-worker FastAPI behind the CDN saturated, requests to /members timed out or 5xx'd, and the frontend AuthContext previously wiped localStorage token on ANY error from GET /api/auth/me — so the user got silently logged out and the subsequent re-login race with the proxy showed a Cloudflare page. Fix has three prongs: (1) uploads now go to object storage via ImageService.store_bytes and store only a short /api/image/{id} URL on the character, (2) the members-directory route defensively migrates any lingering data: URI it encounters and rewrites the character doc, so payload stays ~36 KB, (3) AuthContext only clears the token on 401/403 — network/timeout/5xx keep the session intact. All three verified.
